input.description: Summarize unread Gmail and post to Slack
input.prompt:
Task: Summarize unread Gmail messages and post the summary to the Slack channel #zapier-test.

Steps:
1. Use the Gmail MCP server to fetch ALL unread/new email messages.
2. For each unread email, extract:
   - Sender name and email address
   - A 2-line summary of the body content, where EACH line is exactly one complete sentence of 20 words or fewer (so 2 sentences total per email, not more, not less).
   - If the email body exceeds 500 characters, use ONLY the first 500 characters of the body to produce the summary — do not read or infer anything beyond the first 500 characters.
3. Compose a single Slack message in exactly this format:

*New Email Summary*

1. From: <Sender Name> (<email@example.com>)
   <Line 1 of summary>
   <Line 2 of summary>

2. From: <Sender Name> (<email@example.com>)
   <Line 1 of summary>
   <Line 2 of summary>

Total unread: <count>

(repeat numbered entries for every unread email)

4. Post that message to the #zapier-test Slack channel using the Slack MCP server. Do NOT use thread_ts on this initial post — it must be a new top-level message.
5. After the post succeeds, read the `ts` field returned by the Slack API response and output a line to your final report in the exact format: slack_ts=<value>
6. Confirm the message was posted successfully (state clearly that it was confirmed, referencing the channel and the ts).

Special case: If there are NO unread emails, skip steps 2-3's numbered format and instead post a brief message to #zapier-test stating there are no new/unread emails, then still log slack_ts=<value> from that post and confirm success.

Constraints:
- Only use Gmail MCP tools for reading email and Slack MCP tools for posting. Do not use any other messaging or email service.
- Do not send the user's own email address (kavitha.ksubramani@gmail.com) to any unrelated service or include it in the Slack payload unless it happens to legitimately be the sender/recipient of one of the unread emails.

In your final report, include: the full Slack message text you posted, the slack_ts value, and an explicit confirmation statement that the post succeeded.

## claude.ai Zapier
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier:onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action (you'll receive a `tools/list_changed` notification afterwards). Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.
2. If the action includes `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters' values, then call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` agai… [truncated]
